newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Mosel subsidiary seeks US$320m loan.
newsitem.headline: Mosel subsidiary seeks US$320m loan.

text.p: Taiwan's PROMOS Technologies, a subsidiary of chipmaker Mosel Vitelic, said on Monday it planned to seek a US$320 million syndicated loan to fund an ongoing wafer plant project.
The loan would have a seven-year term and bear a loan rate of LIBOR plus 0.525 percentage points, a Mosel spokesman said by telephone.
"We will sign the contract with our lead underwriter, Bank of America, on May 12," Mosel vice president William Chen said.
Chen said PROMOS, owned 62 percent by Mosel and 38 percent by Siemens AG, planned to use the money to fund its wafer plant in the northern Hsinchu science park.
The plant is expected to begin producing 64 megabit and 256 megabit dynamic random access memory chips in mid-1997.
PROMOS had said it expected the plant's monthly production capacity to reach 20,000 DRAM wafers by the end of 1997 and 40,000 wafers by end-1998.
